transcript.content: Hello, how are you doing today? What brings you in to see me?

Not too good, I guess. I came in because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It’s like… I don’t know, like the old Ruben—me, you know, the guy who could talk to anybody, make a sale, enjoy his day—is just gone.

I used to be pretty good with people, that was kind of my whole thing in sales. I could walk into a place and get a conversation going about anything—weather, baseball, some guy’s kid in college—and now I wake up and it’s just this weight sitting there before I even get moving.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, like activities or interactions that used to make you happy?

Yeah… yeah, I have. I mean, I used to look forward to things. Bowling night, messing around in the garden, taking my wife to those little gallery shows she likes—half the time I didn’t even understand the paintings, but I liked being there with her. We used to go dancing sometimes too.

Now I just… sit there. I’ll come up with some excuse, like I’m tired or it’s too much trouble, and maybe sometimes that’s true, but mostly it just doesn’t feel worth the effort anymore. Even things I know I used to enjoy, they feel kind of empty now.
Has this heavy or empty feeling in your chest stayed with you most of the day, nearly every day, or does it come and go more randomly?

Most days, yeah. It’s there when I wake up, that heavy, hollow thing in my chest, and it kind of sets the tone before I even get dressed. I’ll be brushing my teeth thinking, “Come on, Ruben, you’ve got customers to call,” and then I remember how I used to be able to talk to anybody, just easy, like breathing.

Now it’s like that guy’s not around. I mean, it might lift a little here and there if something distracts me, but it’s not really random. It’s been with me most days.
Have you been feeling fatigued or like you don’t have much energy most days, even when you haven’t done anything physically or mentally taxing?

I… I don’t know, honestly. Tired, sure, but it’s hard for me to tell what’s “energy” and what’s just not wanting to get moving, you know?

Some mornings I’m just standing there in the kitchen staring at the coffee maker, and I start thinking about this customer I used to call on down in Fresno—guy could talk your ear off about boat engines, even though he sold office supplies—and I’d somehow have the patience for it back then. Now I don’t know if I’m physically worn out or just… not there the way I used to be. So I guess I’ve noticed something, but I’m not sure how to answer it exactly.
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not worth much or that you’re failing at things you used to handle easily?

Yeah… I do. More than I want to admit.

I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like, I spent all those years taking care of clients, knowing who liked a call in the morning and who didn’t want to be bothered till after lunch—there was this one account, they’d only talk business after asking about my wife’s tomato plants, can you believe that? And I remembered all that stuff. I was good at it.

But now it’s like none of that counts because I can’t even handle the job the way I used to. And then I think, well, what good am I if I can’t provide, if I can’t keep up? It feels like I’m failing at the one thing I was supposed to know how to do.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like not feeling hungry or losing weight without trying?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I eat, but I haven’t been paying close attention to it. My wife will ask if I want dinner and sometimes I just kind of… shrug, but then other times I’ll pick at something.

Weight-wise, I don’t know. I haven’t been on a scale. My belt feels the same, I think. Though that reminds me, I used to stop at this little place between calls—best pastrami sandwich, they knew me by name—and now I don’t really make those stops like I used to. But I couldn’t tell you if that means anything. I just haven’t noticed a big change.
Would you say that most days, your mood feels significantly low or sad for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… most days, yes.

That’s kind of why I came in, I guess. I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest before the day even starts. It’s not just a bad morning, it’s like… the old Ruben, the one who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy being out in the world, he’s just gone somewhere.

I used to get in the car and know which client was going to joke around, which one needed me to get straight to the point—there was a rhythm to it. Now I wake up and it just feels low, like everything’s already been drained out before I’ve even done anything. So, yeah… I’d say it’s there most of the day, most days.
Have you noticed yourself moving or thinking more slowly than usual lately, like everything’s kind of slowed down?

I don’t know… slowed down how, exactly?

I mean, I’m not as quick to jump up and get moving as I used to be, but I can’t tell if that’s what you mean or if you mean like talking slower or thinking slower. Sometimes I’ll be sitting there and my wife says something and I have to ask her again, but then again she’ll ask me when I’m reading the paper—well, not really reading it, more just holding it—and I’ve always been someone who needed a minute if I was concentrating.

Back when I was driving between clients, I had the whole day mapped out in my head, like who was where and which route would save me ten minutes. There was this one stretch by the old hardware store where traffic would back up every Thursday for no reason at all. I still don’t know why Thursday. But I don’t really… I haven’t been paying attention to whether I’m slower. I guess I’m not sure.
Have you noticed that your thoughts feel slowed down, or that you're moving more slowly than usual, like everything takes extra effort or time?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean… things feel harder to start, but I don’t know if I’m actually moving slower, like if someone watching me would say that.

My wife might have an opinion on that—she notices everything. She’ll tell me I’m standing in the kitchen with the cabinet open, and I’ll be thinking I was just about to get a mug, but then I’m remembering this customer I used to see who collected mugs from every state. Had a whole wall of them, even had Delaware twice for some reason.

So… I don’t know. It feels like stuff takes more out of me, but I can’t really say my thoughts or movements are slowed down in a clear way.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even things that used to be fun or interesting to you?

Yeah… yeah, I have.

I used to really look forward to bowling night. I wasn’t any kind of pro or anything, but I had my ball, my shoes, the whole little routine. There was this guy, Marty, always swore the lane was tilted if he had a bad game, which doesn’t even make sense, but he’d say it every week like it was new. I used to laugh at that.

And the garden too… I’d be out there messing with the tomatoes or trimming things back, and I liked seeing something actually grow because of something I did. My wife would want to go to gallery shows, or sometimes we’d go dancing—nothing fancy, just moving around and feeling like we were still… I don’t know, still us.

Now she’ll suggest something, and I just sit there. I come up with reasons not to go. Too tired, too much traffic, maybe next weekend. But really, it’s just… none of it feels worth the effort anymore. Even the things that used to be fun feel like a chore before I even start.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even things that might not be your fault?

Yeah… I do. More than I probably should.

I keep telling myself I’m useless now. Like, I spent all those years taking care of clients, making sure people got what they needed, keeping accounts straight in my head… I knew everybody’s little preferences, too. There was one guy who wouldn’t meet before 10 because he said coffee didn’t start working till then, and I’d just build the whole route around that.

And I provided for my family. That was… that was what I did. But now it’s like none of that counts because I can’t even handle this job anymore. I just sit there thinking, what good am I if I can’t do the thing I’m supposed to do? So yeah, I blame myself. A lot.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down, lost interest in things, or struggled to feel like yourself?

I don’t know… not really in a way I can point to.

I mean, everybody has rough stretches, right? There were times after a bad quarter at work, or when things were tight, I’d feel worn down for a while. I remember one winter I barely wanted to go anywhere, but then again it was freezing and the roads were a mess—my old car didn’t heat right on the passenger side, which drove my wife crazy.

But episodes like this… where I really felt like I wasn’t myself? I’m not sure. I don’t want to say yes if it was just regular life stuff, you know? This feels different, but I couldn’t give you some clear past time that was the same.
Have you ever had a period of time in the past when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble feeling like yourself for more than just a few days?

I’m not sure… I know you’re asking more than a few days, and I keep trying to think back, but it’s hard to separate things out.

There were bad weeks here and there, sure. Everybody gets those. Like after a rough stretch at work, or if money was tight, I’d get quiet and not want to do much. But then something would come up—yard work, a customer I liked seeing, some stupid joke at the bowling alley—and I’d kind of move along.

I don’t know that I can say there was a real period before where it was like this. Nothing I can clearly point to and say, yes, that was the same thing.
Have you ever had a time in the past when you felt down, lost interest in things, or struggled to feel like yourself for two weeks or more at a time?

Two weeks or more… I don’t know. I really don’t.

I can remember stretches where I was kind of low, but I don’t think I ever marked it on a calendar or anything. Back when I was driving routes, one week would blur into the next sometimes, especially if I was covering for somebody else. I’d be tired, maybe not as social, but then there’d be a decent call with a customer or I’d stop at that diner off Route 6—best pie they had was lemon meringue, though my wife always said it was too sweet—and I’d perk up some.

So… I can’t honestly say there was a clear two-week period like that before. Not one I know for sure.
Have you ever had multiple separate periods in your life when you felt down, lost interest in things, or struggled to feel like yourself, even if they didn’t last as long as this current one?

Multiple separate periods… I’m not sure I’d put it that way.

I mean, I’ve had times where I was off, sure. Everybody does, I guess. Some months just feel heavier than others—work slows down, bills pile up, somebody at home is upset, and then you’re just kind of dragging through it. But I don’t know if those were separate “periods” like you mean.

It’s hard for me to sort it out looking back. A lot of it just feels like regular life getting on top of you, not… whatever this is now. So I can’t really say yes. I don’t have a clear list of times like that.
Have you ever had more than one time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for a while, even if they weren’t as long or severe as this current period?

I don’t really know. I keep trying to line it up in my head, like “was there another time, and another time,” but it all gets mixed together.

I’ve had bad spells, sure. Like, there was that one winter where work was slow and I remember sitting around more than usual… but then I also remember my neighbor asking me to help fix his snowblower, and we ended up spending half the day out there because he had the wrong spark plug, and—anyway, I don’t know if that counts as feeling down for a while or just being annoyed and tired.

So I can’t honestly say there’s been more than one real time like this. Not that I can point to clearly.
Have you had more than one time in the past when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least a couple of weeks at a time?

I still don’t know how to answer that cleanly. More than one time, and for a couple weeks… I can’t really say yes to that.

I’ve had rough patches, like I said, but when you ask “at least a couple weeks,” my head starts trying to sort years like boxes in the garage, and then I remember other things mixed in—work stuff, family stuff, little moments where I wasn’t down the whole time. So… no, not that I can clearly remember. I just don’t have a solid answer for more than one time like that.
Have you ever had more than one time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least a couple of weeks at a time?

I know you’re asking it pretty straight, and I’m probably making it harder than it needs to be, but… I don’t know. I can’t really pick out more than one time like that.

There were stretches where I wasn’t myself, I guess, but then I start thinking, well, was that because business was bad, or because I was tired, or because it was winter—my wife always says I get quieter when it gets dark early, but she says that about everybody in the house, even the dog gets lazy then. So I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

At least a couple weeks… maybe? But I can’t say it for sure. Nothing I can clearly point to and say, yes, that happened more than once.
Can you recall having more than one time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks at a time?

I’m sorry, I know I keep circling this, but I really can’t recall it in a way that feels definite. More than one time for two weeks or more… I don’t have a clear “yes” for that.

I can remember being low here and there, or not wanting to do much, but then I start thinking about what was going on at the time—work being weird, weather, family stuff—and it all sort of blurs together. Like, I’ll remember one bad week and then suddenly I’m thinking about some customer from years ago who used to call every Friday, and it pulls me away from the actual question.

So… I guess the honest answer is I’m not sure. I can’t point to more than one separate stretch like that.
Can you recall having more than one time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks at a time?

I guess I still can’t really say, doctor. I know you’re asking if it happened more than once and lasted two weeks, but when I try to think back, it gets kind of muddy.

There were times I wasn’t doing great, sure, but then I start wondering if that was just stress or just normal life stuff. I remember little pieces more than whole stretches, if that makes sense. Like I can picture where I was working, or what was going on at home, but not cleanly enough to say, “yes, that was two weeks, and yes, it happened again.”

So… I don’t have a clear answer for more than one time. I’m not sure.
